content.comment_body: Hello, How can I set negative values for the analog simulation value? The interface only allows input between 0.0 and 1000.00. Any guidance would be appreciated. Thank you. --- This post was separated from the previous thread about smoothing and combining analog signals in [product_name] [version_no].

I'm not sure I understand your question fully. If you are referring to the analog input, only values between 0 and 1000 are accepted. Could you share a screenshot of your configuration? Edit: @moderator: I can't use the "Suggestion" button. Could you split this into a separate topic?

Hi, In your example, you've set AI2 simulation value to a negative number, right? When I try to replicate this in my setup, I see the same message regarding allowed values. How did you enable negative values?
As mentioned earlier: The analog input only accepts values between 0 and 1000. Edit: @moderator: I'm unable to view the images in the above post, only the attachments are visible.
Here is the screenshot of your configuration.
Check the image. If you want to use negative values, you need to adjust the related parameter in the amplifier settings.
Got it—issue solved. Thank you for your help!

analysis.insight_summary: The primary concern discussed is the system's restriction on analog simulation values, only accepting inputs between 0.0 and 1000.00. Users wanted to enable negative values but were blocked by these limitations. Resolution came by altering a specific amplifier parameter, clarifying how negative values can be configured through the software settings.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the configuration software to permit direct input of negative analog values or allow for adjustments so the accepted range matches practical requirements.
